newsitem.title: UK: LME copper ends slightly weaker in late trading.
newsitem.headline: LME copper ends slightly weaker in late trading.

text.p: Copper prices drifted lower in late inter-office trading on Monday, compounding the weaker sentiment seen on the market during the day's disappointing session.
Traders commented on a lack of follow-through buying when prices reached a peak of $2,390 a tonne after the day's earlier flurry based on talk of Chinese buying.
At 1900 GMT three months prices were indicated at $2,361/63 after finishing the kerb at $2,367 a tonne, down just $1 from Friday's kerb close.

"The poor close is suggestive of further selling pressure but with the technical indicators maintaining their upward trend, we would look for further dips to provide buying opportunities with stops below $2,350," said Rudolf Wolff in its evening metal report.

LME warehouse stocks are expected to fall again on Tuesday as more copper is shipped out of Singapore. Traders said some some 25,000 tonnes of metal may be lifted from this location in the coming week.
Aluminium followed the tone set by copper and was indicated at $1,651/53 after finishing at $1,657, unchanged from Friday. Earlier it saw a test of $1,670.

Nickel continued to move lower and was indicated at $7,780/85, compared with a kerb close of $7,820 which was $135 lower than Friday. Wolff said a test of initial support at $7,750 could be expected, followed by $7,620.
Other metals were little changed to slightly lower.
